te: Meeting with the Chinese Defence Attaché prepared, and the Bureau of the Budget invited to explain disaster relief budgets
se: The meeting considered a call on the Defence Attaché of the People's Republic of China to Thailand on 24 January 2025, a study visit to the Government Lottery Office, and inviting representatives of the Bureau of the Budget to explain the framework of budget support for disaster prevention and mitigation under agencies' missions
it: Call on the Chinese Defence Attaché to Thailand for discussions
Study visit and discussions at the Government Lottery Office
Budget framework for disaster prevention and mitigation

te: Issues prepared for discussion with the Chief of Defence Forces
se: The meeting set issues for discussion with the Chief of Defence Forces, such as using reserve forces to support disaster relief, expanding the military cyber centre into a military cyber command, the joint staff course, the effects of restructuring the Ministry of Defence, and the role of Royal Thai Armed Forces Headquarters in relation to the deployment of armed groups in the area of the Thai–Myanmar border
it: Issues for discussion with the Chief of Defence Forces

te: Study visit plan for early 2025 approved, and agencies to be invited on Ko Kut
se: The meeting approved a plan of study visits in January 2025, such as to the headquarters of the Royal Thai Army, the Royal Thai Air Force, the Royal Thai Armed Forces and the 3th Army Area, and a framework for visits abroad in mid-2025. It agreed to invite energy, defence, security, military survey and treaty agencies to give information on the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut, resolved to invite the Royal Thai Navy, the Institute of Forensic Medicine and the training unit to give further information on the death of a conscript, approved a forum on security research technology, and assigned the Subcommittee on Holistic Security to study the Thai–Cambodian maritime zones and land title documents in Ko Kut District
it: Plan for domestic study visits (January 2025) and a framework for visits abroad
The area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut
The death of a conscript during training
Forum on security research technology and new forms of threat

te: Maritime and border security discussed, and regular situation reports requested
se: The meeting discussed important security situations: the incident involving Thai fishing boats in the Andaman Sea near Myanmar's zone, the situation along the northern border, and the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. .... It agreed that intelligence agencies should report on situations affecting security every two weeks and that members should travel to hear agencies directly. It approved the Subcommittee on Military Affairs' study visit to the East, and noted that the Subcommittee on Cyber, Technology, Weapons and Defence Industry is studying legal obstacles facing the defence industry, such as the firearms law and the law on private weapons factories
it: Maritime and border security situation
Study visit on military affairs in the East (8–10 January 2025)
Legal obstacles facing the defence industry

te: Study visit on the defence industry prepared, and complaints on peace in the southern border provinces received
se: The meeting approved a trip to hear about defence industry capabilities in Khlong Luang District, Pathum Thani Province, on 13 December 2024, noted the outcome of a courtesy call on the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, and considered 2 complaints: a proposal that the government solve national problems, and a proposal on approaches to building peace in the southern border provinces. It also received reports from the subcommittees, such as a study of approaches to developing conscripts into community leaders after discharge, and a framework for studying the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut
it: Trip to hear about defence industry capabilities (13 December 2024)
Outcome of the courtesy call on the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence
2 complaints (national problems · peace in the southern border provinces)
Subcommittee reports: developing conscripts into community leaders · the area of overlapping claims between Thailand and Cambodia around Ko Kut

te: Subcommittees' work followed up, from veterans' entitlements to the draft Ministry of Defence law
se: The meeting received a report from the Subcommittee on Military Affairs, which is following the death of a conscript while awaiting the Royal Thai Navy's official explanation, and is studying online applications for conscript service, the physical fitness test manual, using reserve forces to help with disaster relief, and veterans' benefits, and has set up a working group to prepare views on the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. .... The Subcommittee on Holistic Security is considering requests from local administrative organisations in the southern border provinces so that they are in line with the law, and is preparing issues for discussion with the Minister of Defence
it: Report of the Subcommittee on Military Affairs: recruitment, reserve forces and veterans' entitlements
Working group to prepare views on the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. ....
Report of the Subcommittee on Holistic Security

te: Framework set for inviting persons to give information, and subcommittees' work plans received
se: The meeting noted the orders setting up 3 subcommittees, the Cabinet resolution on the draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. ...., and the schedule of a courtesy call on the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence. It approved a framework for summoning documents or inviting persons to state facts under section 129 of the Constitution and the Senate Rules of Procedure, and received the subcommittees' work plans, such as preparing personnel for cyber and artificial intelligence, promoting the private sector in the defence industry, and preparing site visits to the southern border provinces
it: Framework for summoning documents or inviting persons to state facts (Constitution, section 129)
Draft Act on the Organisation of the Ministry of Defence (No. ..) B.E. ....
Work plans of 3 subcommittees

te: Outcome of the site visit on the death of a conscript heard, and subcommittee names revised
se: The meeting noted the outcome of site visits to hear the facts at the training unit in Sattahip District and at the home of the family of the conscript who died, in Songkhla Province. It felt that information must be heard from all sides so as to be fair to everyone, and that the responsible agency's fact-finding should first be allowed to complete its process. It also revised the names of the 3 subcommittees to Military Affairs; Cyber, Technology, Weapons and Defence Industry; and Holistic Security, and asked each to begin with urgent work that can show results
it: Progress on the death of a conscript during training
Names, approaches and timeframes of the 3 subcommittees
Approach to allocating the committee's budget for 2025

te: Subcommittees' work plans set, and the death of a conscript during training followed up
se: The meeting set the work plans of 3 subcommittees: holistic security; military affairs, veterans and mobilising resources to help the public; and promoting the defence industry, including proposing amendments to laws that are obstacles. It considered the death of a conscript during training, agreeing that clarity should be established and the family given relief promptly, and assigned committee members to visit and offer support to the family in Songkhla Province and to hear information from the training unit in Sattahip District, Chon Buri Province
it: Work plans of 3 subcommittees
The death of a conscript during training

te: 3 subcommittees set up, and meetings set for every Wednesday
se: The meeting noted that 4 committee members had left office under rule 78, paragraph four, of the Senate Rules of Procedure, a request for information for the 45th General Assembly of the ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly in Lao PDR, and a complaint requesting reinstatement in military service. It considered changes of positions in the committee, set meetings for every Wednesday, and set up 3 subcommittees, on holistic security, military affairs and veterans, and security and defence industries, and heard a lecture on a strategy to drive the defence industry
it: Members leaving office (Rules of Procedure, rule 78, paragraph four) and changes of positions
Setting up 3 subcommittees
Lecture on a strategic concept for driving the defence industry
Complaint requesting fair treatment and reinstatement in military service

te: First meeting after the Senate set up the committee
se: Agenda: first meeting of the committee, after the Senate at its sitting No. 15 on 23 September 2024 resolved to set up the Senate standing committees (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: First meeting of the committee

te: 90 days of work summarised, and a letter asking for help with laws that are obstacles received
se: The meeting considered its work from October to December 2024 and began preparing a report on defence industry capabilities for combat power in all 6 domains and the challenges for the Thai state in the modern world. It considered a letter from an association of business operators asking for help with legal problems, which the committee had assigned the subcommittee to consider first and to invite those concerned for discussion
it: Report on defence industry capabilities for combat power in all 6 domains
Letter asking for help with legal problems that are obstacles to the defence industry

te: Reports to be completed by March 2025, and a study visit to a Thai drone maker noted
se: The meeting noted that the Chair of the committee had asked every subcommittee to submit its reports by March 2025 so they can go to the Senate before the session closes, considered representatives to help prepare the committee's annual report, and noted the outcome of the study visit on 13 December 2024 to Thai businesses working on drones and security systems
it: Deadline for submitting study reports (by March 2025)
Outcome of the study visit to businesses working on drones and security systems

te: Laws that are obstacles to the defence industry reviewed
se: The meeting considered laws relating to the defence industry, such as the law on private weapons factories, the law on the control of military equipment, the defence technology law and the firearms law, observing that some are not in line with present conditions and are obstacles for Thai businesses, and agreed to invite the Defence Industry and Energy Center, the Department of Foreign Trade and the Department of Provincial Administration to give information
it: Legal obstacles facing the defence industry

te: The defence industry under the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy
se: The meeting considered approaches to developing Thailand's defence industry under the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy, with a focus on self-reliance and personnel development, observing that it should begin by encouraging the armed forces to use equipment made in Thailand, to build international confidence in Thai equipment
it: Approaches to developing the defence industry under the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy

te: Outcome of discussions with the Minister of Defence on raising the defence industry to international level noted
se: The meeting noted the outcome of its discussion with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence on 13 November 2024 on developing and raising the defence industry to international level. They agreed to promote production in Thailand for employment and knowledge transfer, developing step by step, and the Ministry of Defence is ready to support the armed forces' research
it: Outcome of the discussion with the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence
